estate._comment: The devices senechal is majordomo of. One place a new device gets added; health/*.sh read this, never their own host lists. owner = who fixes problems in that device's domain; senechal owns the gaps. See ESTATE.md for prose.
estate._footprint_comment: Registered machine-config footprint: things some project installed on some host that outlive the session that installed them. senechal owns KNOWING these exist (see CLAUDE.md's notify-senechal protocol) -- and, since 2026-07-28, noticing when one has become a corpse. health/dead-config.sh probes each entry read-only and never removes anything; removal is human-confirmed by contract. status: live (should be here and working) / retiring (agreed dead, still installed -- nagged every run until gone) / retired (should be absent -- flagged loudly if it comes back). kind: systemd-system-unit, systemd-user-unit, listening-port, path, authorized-keys. target is kind-specific; retire is the exact command that finishes the job.
estate._taste_comment: A 'taste' is a Zach shell/config preference that should be applied identically on every home he has a shell on, and re-applied without duplicating itself if the target file gets hand-edited. The mechanism, not just this one entry: lib/taste-block.sh installs/verifies a marker-delimited block in a file; remedies/<id>.sh reads this list's `hosts` for its own id, resolves each host to local-vs-ssh via estate.devices, and applies/checks the block there. Onboarding a NEW home (Zach's 'movement across homes') is adding its name to a taste's `hosts` array here plus a device entry above -- no script change. file is ~-relative, same value on every host (each remote resolves its own ~). status: enabled (should be installed everywhere in hosts) / disabled (should be ABSENT everywhere -- not used yet, no taste has been retired). See CONCERNS.md for the per-taste writeup.

secrets.notes: CORRECTED 2026-08-13: an earlier entry called this NOT re-mintable. It is. GitHub Apps allow generating additional private keys and deleting old ones; the App and its installations survive. That correction removes the only argument for keeping a plaintext off-host copy, so this is now offhost=forbid like the rest. Discogs personal access token -- https://www.discogs.com/settings/developers , Generate new token, and revoke the old one there. The catalog writeback URL is a wtul endpoint rather than a third-party credential; ask wtul. Write all three back into this file, one per line, and chmod 600.

taste.description: PS1 colors \u and \h with two INDEPENDENT hashes (not one hash of the combined string), so a familiar user on an unfamiliar host (or vice versa) is visible at a glance without reading it; @ stays uncolored. Computed live at shell start, so one identical block works unmodified on every host.
taste.notes: Filed via `scheduler -i` 2026-07-29 22:44 (.scheduler/FOCUS.md): 'bashrc that makes user and host colors hashes of ids ... install on all systems'. Content and remedy: remedies/colorhash-prompt.sh (config edit to Zach's shell -- preference decision, so it ships as enable/verify per CLAUDE.md's acting-authority rules, not applied unattended). Still declares `hosts`, deliberately unmigrated: cfg_taste reads it as shorthand for zach@<host>, which is what it always meant.

taste.description: Zach's interactive Claude slash commands (/bashify, /cloture, /ideate) present and CURRENT in every home he might type them in. Content is generated by realisateur's bin/install-shims.sh from its own .claude/commands/*.md (every file declaring `scope: user`); senechal does not hold a copy and never will -- it asserts the estate-wide property realisateur's own --check cannot see, because that check only ever inspects the host it runs on.
taste.notes: Zach 2026-08-06: these belong in every home where he might interactively call an agent -- every zach@ account, and anywhere the hf7y verb build lands -- and they must be tracked by something OTHER than `installe`. installe owns PATH symlinks out of a verb build (~/.local/bin/<verb> -> verb-builds/current/..., retired via `installe retire <verb>`); slash commands are a different artifact class with a different lifecycle: per-home files under ~/.claude/commands/, needed in homes that may have no verb build at all. Routing them through installe would mean inventing a fake verb and coupling 'Zach can type /ideate here' to 'this account has a build'. Hence this registry. `homes` (not `hosts`) because monkey carries one UNIX account per self-dev project plus zach as the hands account, and only zach@monkey wants these -- the other nine run agents non-interactively. Remedy: remedies/claude-slash-commands.sh; verify is wired into health/estate-health.sh. State when filed 2026-08-06: drifted on mandark, stale hand-copy on dexter, entirely absent in zach@monkey.
taste.owner: realisateur (generates and owns the command content) / senechal (owns knowing WHICH homes need them and whether they are current there)
